items.question: How should a stock-flow model account for offered work at every integration step?

section_new.excerpt: ## Case 1: conservation The stock-flow model must preserve: offered = completed + rejected + backlog The test runs a below-capacity case, a saturation case and a zero-arrival case. It checks the identity at every step and refuses a negative backlog. A broken service calculation usually shows up as a conservation gap or a negative stock. The observed results are in the order-intake baseline and saturation runs. The baseline has zero rejection and zero backlog; the saturation case has 0.2 rejection, a 77.6-request backlog and a 24-request-per-second throughput.
section_new.heading: Case 1: conservation

items.question: How does the V12 event queue break ties between events scheduled at the same time?

section_new.excerpt: ## Failure modes - **Unstable tie-breaking.** Two events at the same time depend on hash order. - **Timeout resets on retry omitted.** A retry inherits an expired deadline and fails immediately. - **Timeout not cancelled on completion.** A completed request is later marked failed. - **Double release.** A timeout and a completion both free the same server, increasing capacity beyond the configured pool. - **Floating-point equality.** Events at 1.0 and 1.0000000001 are treated as equal or not equal without a declared tolerance. V12 rounds scheduled times to 12 decimal places and compares event times as floats. That is sufficient for the synthetic scenarios; a model with very small time units w
section_new.heading: Failure modes

items.question: What happens to the timeout when the V12 discrete-event model retries an attempt?

section_new.excerpt: ## Diagram ~~~mermaid sequenceDiagram participant A as Arrival participant Q as Queue participant S as Server participant T as Timeout A->>Q: admit or reject Q->>S: dispatch when capacity is free S-->>Q: release on completion T-->>S: cancel expired attempt S-->>A: completed, failed or retried ~~~ Text alternative: an arrival is admitted to a bounded queue or rejected. A free server dispatches a queued request, and completion releases capacity. A timeout can cancel an expired attempt and trigger a bounded retry.

items.question: How does the V12 quadratic sensitivity screen differ from a full Sobol analysis?

section_new.excerpt: ## Evidence and limits The source ledger records the exact unit, representation hash, sections read, omissions and limits for each admitted source. The engine tests exercise conservation, boundary cases, event ordering, retries, convergence and sensitivity ranking. Those tests prove the implemented reference cases; they do not validate a real system. All numeric workloads in this volume are synthetic. The confidence intervals use a normal approximation across replications. The sensitivity screen uses a quadratic response-surface decomposition, not a full pick-freeze Sobol analysis. Calibration is `uncalibrated` for every model. Independent review and owner acceptance remain separate decision
section_new.heading: Evidence and limits
